items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee (Dave Brubeck) does not speak in the provided transcript. The mention of 'Butler' refers to Duke Ellington's father, mentioned by the interviewer in a story about Duke Ellington. No personal connection between Dave Brubeck and Butler is established.

ctx.x: You play maybe three or four. The Ellington night, there’s so many jazz musicians that you just go up and play one tune. When I think of the Ellington night, I think of the night that I really liked Dick Nixon, who I hadn’t been a fan of. But he said – we’re at the dinner in a separate room. He gets up to make a speech of welcome. He said, “In this room there’s been welcome and entertainment for kings and queens and leaders of the world, but tonight we entertain our first Duke.” Then he said, “It’s come full…

“. . . butler in this room. Tonight we’re entertaining and honoring his son.” Isn’t that great? It was so wonderful. Iola was sitting with Mercer [Ellington] in a room full of musicians and great statesmen. I don’t know why I got on that, but I was thinking of how great that was, Duke being raised in Washington.
